page: Amazon Web Services g4dn.2xlarge is an accelerated computing instance provisioned on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. A discrete NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM provides dedicated hardware acceleration. Local ephemeral storage is bundled via a 225 GB NVMe SSD, and baseline network performance is rated at 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data demonstrates marked differences between CPU execution and GPU acceleration. Central processing scores show modest compute capability, with stress-ng single-core (1284.59) and Geekbench scores (1125.0 single-core, 4267.0 multi-core) placing in the lower quartile. Similarly, sequential compression benchmarks such as single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression register in the weak tier. System memory and multi-core throughput operate near median averages, showing 50.58 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 38.12 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth, and 6.7 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary operational strength of the instance lies in machine learning inference workloads handled by the NVIDIA T4 GPU. In small 135M parameter LLM evaluation, prompt processing reaches 8454.68 tokens per second (top tier) with text generation achieving 296.67 tokens per second. For medium 7B models, prompt processing delivers 1151.25 tokens per second (top tier) alongside text generation speeds of 41.93 tokens per second. Memory constraints on the 16 GB GPU preclude large 70B parameter models without model distribution across instances.

Cost efficiency is centered around lightweight GPU-accelerated inference and graphics rendering tasks rather than raw host CPU computations. For organizations seeking localized NVMe scratch space and dedicated hardware acceleration without paying for large multicore CPU topologies or high-end accelerator tiers, this instance represents a balanced entry point. It is best matched to machine learning model inference, video transcoding, graphics workstations, and GPU-driven pipeline tasks.
